Step 1: Calculate the total distance Jon drives in the 30-day month. He drives 100 miles a day, so for 30 days, the total mileage is $100 \text{ miles/day} \times 30 \text{ days} = 3000 \text{ miles}$.

Step 2: Determine how often Jon's car needs a tune-up. The car needs a tune-up every 1000 miles.

Step 3: Calculate the number of tune-ups needed by dividing the total distance driven by the mileage interval for a tune-up: $3000 \text{ miles} / 1000 \text{ miles/tune-up} = 3 \text{ tune-ups}$.

Final answer: 3
